scenes.name: Soul jazz: órgano Hammond y guitarra
scenes.author: Ted Gioia
scenes.desc: El hard bop impregnado de gospel y rhythm and blues que Alfred Lion no quería publicar y acabó explotando: ritmos binarios y cuaternarios guturales, llamada y respuesta, blues, la herencia de los tenores tejanos y de Kansas City y las batallas de saxos (Lockjaw Davis y Johnny Griffin). Su voz es el órgano Hammond B-3: tras Bill Doggett y Wild Bill Davis, Jimmy Smith lo impone en Blue Note con blues de veinte minutos («The Sermon»); le siguen Jimmy McGriff, Jack McDuff, Shirley Scott o Groove Holmes, y Larry Young lo lleva a Coltrane y a la fusión de Lifetime. En la guitarra, Kenny Burrell (Midnight Blue) y Wes Montgomery, autodidacta que toca con el pulgar y en octavas y acaba vendiendo millones con versiones de los Beatles. Motown, el funk y el soul le quitan el público negro a finales de los sesenta.

podcast.title: Collaborative Recording with Bill Doggett
podcast.body: Wild Bill Davis rejoined Louis Jordan's band to record "Tambor Ritz a Boogey," playing the Hammond organ alongside Bill Doggett on piano. This close interaction further fascinated Doggett with the instrument. "When Dogget left Jordan's band, he decided to form an organ trio, just like Davis's."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Inspiration for Bill Doggett's Organ Trio
podcast.body: After leaving Louis Jordan's band, Bill Doggett decided to form his own organ trio, directly inspired by Wild Bill Davis's successful model, though their similar instrumentation and playing styles initially led to comparisons. "When Dogget left Jordan's band, he decided to form an organ trio, just like Davis's."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Pioneering Hammond Organ Jazz Trio
podcast.body: Wild Bill Davis was a pioneer in exploring the possibilities of the Hammond organ as a musical instrument, forming a trio consisting of himself on organ, a guitarist, and a drummer, specifically to exploit its potential in jazz music. "Davis had discovered the possibilities in a new musical instrument, the Hammond organ, and had formed a trio consisting of himself, a guitarist, and the drummer, to exploit these possibilities in jazz music."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Shaping Hammond Organ Prominence
podcast.body: Alongside Bill Doggett, Wild Bill Davis was instrumental in giving the Hammond organ its prominent place in the worlds of jazz, R&B, and soul music, by developing a new style of keyboard playing for the emerging music of the late 1940s and early 1950s. "Davis and Dogget between them gave the Hammond organ its prominence in the world of jazz, R&B, and Soul Music."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
